summary: Order placement 500s on order-service are caused (H1, confidence 0.85, high) by the v2.14.0 deployment dep-5101 (2026-03-03T12:10:00Z), which introduced a new MarginCheckValidator in the validation chain and removed the legacy OrderRules.validateMargin(); the validator throws a NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 when marginProfile is null for F&O (derivatives) orders. The failure is an immediate synchronous NPE in the derivatives path only, appearing at the 12:12Z onset bucket ~2 minutes after the deploy, while traffic (~232 req/s), CPU (~40%), memory (~60%) and db_pool_in_use (~14) are all flat, and no other service deployed or changed config in the window. Alternative hypotheses (pricing-engine/downstream data, resource exhaustion, TLS/DNS/network) are contradicted by the evidence and rejected. Remaining uncertainty is limited to confirmatory gaps (no rollback yet, downstream telemetry not queried), which do not change the origin of the fault.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.14.0 regression: new MarginCheckValidator crashes on null marginProfile for F&O orders
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deployment dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0, 12:10:00Z) replaced the legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() with a new MarginCheckValidator in the validation chain; the new validator throws a NullPointerException at line 88 when marginProfile is null for FNO (derivatives) orders, producing immediate HTTP 500 rejections on the derivatives order path only. Origin: order-service's own code, introduced by dep-5101.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0) deployed at 2026-03-03T12:10:00Z introduces 'new MarginCheckValidator in validation chain' and removes legacy OrderRules.validateMargin(); it is the only change (deploy or config) anywhere in the window.
Onset of the error-rate plateau (0.2% -> ~18%) begins in the 12:10-12:12Z window, ~2 min after the deploy, with the first ERROR at 12:12:31Z.
Errors are dominated by NullPointerException in MarginCheckValidator.validate line 88 with 'marginProfile is null for account', orderType=FNO only.

Failures are immediate and synchronous inside the validator (no upstream-call frame, no timeout/latency signature), and only the FNO path through MarginCheckValidator is affected — a hard 500 rejection.
The failing slice is a stable ~18% of unchanged total traffic (~232 req/s), matching the FNO share of orders, and persists as a plateau through 13:56Z with no recovery.
order-service resources (CPU ~40%, memory ~60%, db_pool_in_use ~14) show no degradation at onset, excluding a resource/latency mechanism.
Blast radius is derivatives-only, which shared datastore/cache/queue dependencies (shared:true) would not produce.

assumptions: The ~18% error fraction corresponds to the FNO share of order volume (the exact non-FNO error count is not visible due to truncated logs).

The validator throws before any downstream call, so a null marginProfile reaching it originates in data the new code fails to handle rather than in a downstream dependency response that would leave an upstream-call frame.
dep-5101 rolled out to the whole fleet (rollout percentage unknown; rolled_back_at is null).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Pricing-engine (or margin/valuation dependency) returns missing/null marginProfile for F&O, breaking the order path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A downstream dependency that supplies margin data — pricing-engine (shared:false, http from order-service) or an upstream valuation/risk component feeding it — began returning responses without a marginProfile for derivatives accounts, and the margin check then fails, surfacing as 500s at order-service. Origin: the downstream dependency, not order-service code.

causal_chain.claim: pricing-engine is http-reachable from order-service and is the only non-shared cost-path dependency plausibly exercised more by F&O orders.
Pricing/valuation data for F&O accounts became null or absent, so no marginProfile is available at validation time.
The margin check (new or legacy) then fails on the null marginProfile, producing a 500 on the FNO order path.

assumptions: pricing-engine (or a component feeding it) degraded at ~12:10-12:12Z without any deploy or config change (none found for it in 11:00Z-14:00Z).
The NPE frame in MarginCheckValidator is downstream of a dependency call that left no visible frame in the sampled logs.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The failure is an immediate synchronous NPE with no upstream-call frame, no timeout and no latency component, which a downstream pricing/valuation degradation would not produce; pricing-engine had zero deployments/config changes in 11:00Z-14:00Z; and the only change touching the failing code path explicitly introduces the validator that throws. Downstream telemetry was not queried, but every available signal points away from pricing-engine.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / pool or capacity saturation on order-service or shared datastore after a traffic or retry surge
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A derivatives-driven load increase (or client retry storm following initial failures) exhausted a connection/thread pool or saturated a shared datastore (ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka), causing 500s on the derivatives order path. Origin: resource/capacity limits, not code.

causal_chain.claim: Derivatives order volume or a post-failure retry storm increased pressure on connection/thread pools or the shared datastore.
Pool/connection exhaustion would surface as 'connection is not available' / pool-exhausted errors or elevated latency and db_pool_in_use.
Exhausted resources then cause 500s on the affected path.

assumptions: cpu/memory/db_pool_in_use metrics under-report the true pool pressure (not supported by the data).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Total request rate is flat (~232 req/s) with no surge, db_pool_in_use is flat at ~14, CPU ~40% and memory ~60% are unchanged across onset, and the error is a synchronous NullPointerException rather than a pool/latency/timeout signature. The symptom is a stable ~18% slice of steady traffic, not load-driven degradation. HIST-115's pool-misconfig precedent (config_change) is a lead only and matches neither the observed error text nor the absence of any config change.

ranked_hypotheses.title: TLS/certificate, DNS or network-layer failure between order-service and a dependency
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Certificate expiry or a network/DNS/TLS failure on a hop between order-service and a dependency causes connection-level failures that surface as 500s, disproportionately on the derivatives path because that path makes an extra call. Origin: network/credential layer.

causal_chain.claim: A certificate/token expired or DNS/TLS connectivity to a dependency broke at ~12:10Z.
Calls on the affected hop fail, raising 500s on order paths that traverse it (F&O more heavily).

assumptions: A credential expired at exactly the onset window without appearing in any change feed.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: All sampled errors are application-level NullPointerExceptions inside MarginCheckValidator with no TLS, DNS, connection-refused or upstream-timeout frames; failure is immediate and synchronous.
